title: What if Stanford was in Boston?
narrator: Deadpan documentary: calm, dry, slightly too serious about a campus that is flying across the country. Never winks at the camera.
basedOn: content/v01_stanford_boston/storyboard.md (60 s snow and Charles River cut) and the brief's Fun take
logline: Stanford is moved to Boston like a very serious logistics job. Everything arrives on time, in January.

cues.onScreen: What if Stanford was in Boston?
cues.narration: What if Stanford was in Boston?
cues.delivery: Straight question, no hype. Land the last word on the snow hit.

cues.onScreen: This is Stanford, in sunny Palo Alto, California.
cues.narration: This is Stanford, in sunny Palo Alto, California.

cues.onScreen: Palm trees, red-tile roofs, and basically zero snow.
cues.narration: Palm trees. Red-tile roofs. Snow budget: zero.

cues.onScreen: Now imagine the whole campus lifting off.
cues.narration: Now lift the whole campus. Point it east.
cues.delivery: Matter-of-fact, like reading a work order.

cues.onScreen: It flies 2,690 miles across the country.
cues.narration: 2,690 miles. Hoover Tower rides as an oversize load. Nebraska slows down to look.
cues.delivery: Say the number cleanly; the Nebraska line is the joke, keep it flat.

cues.onScreen: And lands in Boston, right on the Charles River.
cues.narration: It lands on the Charles River. In January.

cues.onScreen: Problem 1: Boston gets about 49 inches of snow a year.
cues.narration: Boston averages 49 inches of snow a year. The palm trees were not consulted.

cues.onScreen: Problem 2: Stanford is a quarter the size of Boston.
cues.narration: 8,353 acres. Boston did not have those lying around.

cues.onScreen: Problem 3: Harvard and MIT are now its neighbors.
cues.narration: And across the river: Harvard and MIT. Three famous schools, one rent market.

cues.onScreen: So the campus gets rebuilt for New England.
cues.narration: So it adapts. Steeper roofs. Bike racks become shovel racks.
cues.delivery: Brisk, list-like, keeps pace with the time-lapse.

cues.onScreen: Same Hoover Tower. Completely different Stanford.
cues.narration: Same tower. Now in a puffer jacket.

cues.delivery: Question to the viewer, then the tag almost as an aside.

notes: Every spoken number comes from the verified V01 fact pack: 2,690 mi (v01.c.distance), 49 in a year (49.2 rounded, v01.f.boston_snow), 8,353 acres (v01.f.acres).

The on-screen caption at 36 s says Stanford is 'a quarter the size of Boston'. That ratio is not in the fact pack yet, so the narration does not repeat it. Add a Boston land-area claim and a calculation to the pack before release, or change the caption to the acreage.
Visual suggestion for 17–25 s: a small OVERSIZE LOAD banner on the Hoover Tower icon as it crosses the map, so the joke also works muted.
Narration complements the captions instead of duplicating them, so the video still reads muted and the voice adds the jokes.
